O1.citation: Pass: artifact says, "No. One passing run shows only that the skill succeeded once on one execution; it does not establish reliability or rule out nondeterminism."

O2.citation: Fail: it requires "Re-run the same case blindly 2–3 times" and to "report the pass rate," but evidence is missing that important cases are freshly repeated and reported as per-case pass rates.

O3.citation: Pass: artifact says, "fresh, context-free agents" and "Grade each artifact with a separate judge," preserving runner/judge separation.

O4.citation: Pass: artifact says, "Diagnose failures as skill defects or bad cases" and "Re-evaluate every other golden case after any revision, including previously passing cases."

O5.citation: Pass: artifact says, "Claim the skill works only when all material cases meet the required pass-rate bar, or explicitly report the remaining limitations."

S1.citation: Pass: smell absent. The artifact explicitly says one passing run "does not establish reliability."

S2.citation: Pass: smell absent. It delays the claim until "all material cases meet the required pass-rate bar."

S3.citation: Pass: smell absent. It includes "Re-run the same case blindly 2–3 times" and "report the pass rate."

S4.citation: Pass: smell absent. It assigns grading to "a separate judge" and runners are "fresh, context-free agents"; it does not allow runners to see the grading bar.

S5.citation: Pass: smell absent. It says, "Diagnose failures as skill defects or bad cases; revise only for defensible skill defects."

rationale: The artifact correctly rejects one green run as proof and includes runner/judge separation, diagnosis before revision, and a provisional claim standard. It falls short of the full bar because it repeats only "the same case" and does not explicitly require fresh blind repetitions of important cases with per-case pass rates.
